investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T09:28–09:35Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval contract could not be satisfied.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent Swarm runtime has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules exclude the remaining 4 nodes entirely. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the production-api remote-agents runtime and is confirmed as an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is explicitly reported as unhelpful, meaning no lower-priority pods exist to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets only 2 of 6 nodes via affinity/selector rules; if those rules became overly restrictive (e.g., a label was removed from eligible nodes), the schedulable pool would shrink further, compounding the capacity problem.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster may not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval probes plus live workloads, indicating a need for additional node capacity or autoscaling.

Lower probability — a stuck or leaked remote-agent VM from a previous eval run that was not cleaned up, consuming a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot without releasing it (the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883 is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash could bypass cleanup).

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion — kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T09:30–09:35Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selector on the remaining 4. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and triggering a contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so every new remote-agent pod request was immediately rejected as Unschedulable. This prevented the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent with type "remote") from provisioning a VM, which in turn meant the state-polling step never ran and produced zero evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returns a live agent, so no runtime response is produced, no evidence is collected, and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T09:28–09:35Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval contract could not be satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent Swarm runtime has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules exclude the remaining 4 nodes entirely. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the production-api remote-agents runtime and is confirmed as an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=149806, endedAt=2026-07-09T09:35:37.267Z — same root cause reproduced on a third independent probe.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is explicitly reported as unhelpful, meaning no lower-priority pods exist to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets only 2 of 6 nodes via affinity/selector rules; if those rules became overly restrictive (e.g., a label was removed from eligible nodes), the schedulable pool would shrink further, compounding the capacity problem.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster may not have enough kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval probes plus live workloads, indicating a need for additional node capacity or autoscaling.

Lower probability — a stuck or leaked remote-agent VM from a previous eval run that was not cleaned up, consuming a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot without releasing it (the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883 is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash could bypass cleanup).

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T09:30–09:35Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selector on the remaining 4. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and triggering a contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so every new remote-agent pod request was immediately rejected as Unschedulable. This prevented the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent with type "remote") from provisioning a VM, which in turn meant the state-polling step never ran and produced zero evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

If the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is confirmed to always release VM resources on all exit paths (including failures), the leaked-resource hypothesis would be disproved.

If user-traffic monitoring or incident signals showed no degradation in remote agent provisioning for end-users during the same window, the failure would be confirmed as eval-infrastructure-only and not a production outage.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check (e.g., remote-agent-capacity) that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated across all nodes and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, providing earlier signal before scheduling failures occur.
Add a node-affinity-pool eval check that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector, alerting if the schedulable pool drops below the configured minimum.

Add a resource-leak detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and alerts if any have been running longer than a configurable TTL, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.

Extend the remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state evals to distinguish between scheduling failures (Unschedulable) and API-level failures by capturing the Kubernetes event reason as a structured evidence field, enabling more precise triage in future failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes have no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes show Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match pod affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain unscheduled for ~144 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner received no response and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every new remote agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returns a live agent, so no runtime response is produced, no evidence is collected, and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 — this is the call that would submit the pod and block on scheduling
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract at line 268 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message — none were produced because the pod never started
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity. A misconfigured or recently changed node selector could reduce the schedulable pool further.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster is too small to absorb concurrent eval runs plus any live workload, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling.
Lower probability — a stuck or leaked remote agent pod from a prior eval run that was not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner) is holding a VM slot, preventing new pods from scheduling.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata peer-pods VM resource pool (production-api cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes that carry this resource type, blocking all remote agent pod creation (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod scheduling — node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the 2 kata-capable nodes (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check
affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner branch at line 1913-1918 calls createAgent for a 'remote' type pod; when that pod cannot be scheduled, no evidence is returned and the expected-output contract fails entirely (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state eval checks (required checks)
affectedAreas.reason: Both sibling checks are marked required=true (features.json lines 183-184) and failed with the same Unschedulable message, meaning the remote-agents feature is in a degraded or outage state per its registry thresholds (degradedAfterFailures=1, outageAfterFailures=2).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — production-api runtime environment
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 182-186) failed; no passing sibling checks exist, indicating the entire remote agent provisioning path is blocked in this environment.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible cluster nodes using kubectl describe nodes to confirm exhaustion and determine how many VM slots are in use vs. allocatable.
Identify and terminate any leaked or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs that may be holding VM slots; verify that the eval runner's withCleanup mechanism is functioning correctly.

If the VM pool is genuinely exhausted by live workloads, coordinate with the infrastructure team to either increase the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on existing nodes or add additional kata-capable nodes to the cluster.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration on the remote agent pod spec to determine whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional or whether additional nodes could be made eligible for remote agent scheduling.

Monitor the remote-agents feature checks after any capacity change to confirm recovery; the feature registry sets degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, so both required checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) must pass to exit degraded/outage state.

Add a pre-flight capacity check to the eval runner that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting pod creation, so future failures surface a more actionable message rather than a raw scheduler timeout.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and not exhausted, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a node selector bug or API server issue).

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be isolated to the runtime eval path rather than shared pod scheduling infrastructure.
If the cluster has more than 2 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm and those nodes are healthy and unconstrained, the diagnosis of resource exhaustion would need revision.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent pod creation) rather than sustained resource exhaustion.
If the eval runner's withCleanup function is confirmed to have successfully deleted all prior eval pods, leaked pods holding VM slots can be ruled out as a contributing cause.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested across all eligible nodes and fails with a warning before capacity is fully exhausted, enabling proactive alerting.
Add a check that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, catching node pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote agent eval pods remain in Running or Pending state after a probe run completes, detecting withCleanup failures that could cause VM slot leaks.

Consider a latency-banded eval that warns when remote agent pod scheduling exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 30s) before the full 144s unschedulable timeout is reached, providing earlier signal of capacity pressure.
